scope: Read-only comparison of current macOS and iPadOS working trees; five focused renderer checks executed on this Mac using each platform source set. Localization only was stubbed. No application source edits in this audit.

findings.detail: macOS consumes and removes the pending snapshot even on Cancel or failed restore/open. iPad retains deferred and unsuccessful recovery candidates.
A 44.1 kHz tone rendered at 48 kHz changes after a split at 0.137 s on macOS; iPad shared renderer is sample-identical.
macOS shortens outer fades, removes inner fades and deletes crossfades at a split. iPad preserves each affected curve segment and crossfade.
macOS mono output bypasses pan and mono-source equal-power pan law; iPad folds down the actual panned stereo mix.
macOS supports schema 1 only. iPad writes schema 2 for partial fades and 3 for partial crossfades; those projects cannot open on macOS. iPad projects without these features still use schema 1.
A -60 dBFS target uses the fader mute sentinel on macOS and sets gain to zero. iPad uses pow(10, dB/20). iPad also supports cancellation and precise trimmed-region sample bounds.

findings.kind: implementation gap; new runtime verification pending
findings.detail: iPad routes M4A through container-aware audio preparation for edits, gaps, retiming and multiple tracks. macOS uses direct AVAudioFile. Ordinary M4A passed the earlier portability suite; edited-container parity is not established.

findings.kind: implementation gap; audible gap duration not measured
findings.detail: macOS stops and restarts the playback engine at every loop boundary. iPad uses continuous PCM queues across boundaries.
Both render clip pan and track volume automation. Only iPad exposes their dedicated add/move/delete/clear editors; macOS exposes clip volume automation editing.

findings.kind: performance architecture difference; no new stress benchmark
findings.detail: iPad uses two shared preparation slots, cancellable waveforms, a waveform memory budget, background source verification and asynchronous cache reads. macOS lacks the corresponding bounded preparation subsystem and cold verification remains synchronous.
iPad offers explicit numeric export start/end fields and optional timeline In/Out import. macOS offers whole project or existing In/Out only.

findings.kind: workflow choice, not automatically a defect
findings.detail: iPad Save project as copies all library sources and creates a new project identity. macOS Save As writes a new project file retaining references and identity; portable copying uses Collect Project Media.
iPad detects byte-identical sources by digest, including across folders. macOS recognizes duplicate library imports by normalized path.

limitations: iPad shared sources compiled and run on macOS, not a fresh iPad device or Simulator test.
Static findings were not all exercised through UI. Loop latency, M4A edited-container behavior and batch preparation performance were not measured in this audit.
The full application suites were not rerun. Earlier export/relink verification remains applicable: its source manifest still matches.
